status: declared by the pull request that closes #450, before any score: the twin, the test, the splits and the lag statistic below are fixed here and nothing is tuned on a scored day
decides: nothing: no published declaration, record or live pin changes; adopting the twin is Eleonora's decision under docs/decisions/publish-rule.md and, for the live pin, her own attested approval (docs/decisions/live-pin.md)

twin.name: published_gbm_direct
twin.of: the published distribution model: the 'published' side of final_test_preregistration.CRPS_COMMAND (gbm, the CRPS_FEATURES, conformal_pid_nested calibration, minimum history 61, refit every 21 scored days, the five quantile levels)
twin.only_difference: ml.fit_gradient_boosted_quantiles(training_pairs="direct"): each training target is paired with the feature row it is served at prediction time (its as-of read) instead of the row before it
twin.tuned: nothing: no other setting is touched and the choice of 'direct' is the one the fitter already offers

scoring.note: scored days are before 2026-01-01 (docs/decisions/lockbox.md); the 2026 window and the blind tier are not looked at; the panel is cut at 2025-12-31 before any fit

test.primary: the paired per-day difference CRPS(published) - CRPS(published_gbm_direct) over every scored day, mean and 90% stationary-bootstrap interval (block length 2, 2000 replications, level 0.90, the published CRPS cell's rule); the twin is better under this test when the lower bound is above 0, and worse when the upper bound is below 0; otherwise there is no difference
also: the same difference against as-of persistence: CRPS(persistence) - CRPS(model) for each model, and the twin's gain over persistence minus the published model's
the same difference split by the declared regimes and by the pressure-day types of metadata/evaluation_splits.json, and on the days whose spread exceeds +5 bp and the other days

lag.statistic: the integer k in -3..5 at which the Pearson correlation of the forecast median of day T with the actual spread of day T-k is highest (the smaller k in a tie); reported for the published model, the twin and as-of persistence, all days and by regime
lag.paired: the 90% stationary-bootstrap interval of the difference in best lag, twin minus published, and of the correlation difference at k = 0 and k = 2

turning_point_days.definition: the definition declared in #445 (PR #447, metadata/nowcast.json), restated here: a scored day whose SOFR - IORB moved by at least 2 bp into it from the day before and at least 2 bp the other way out of it to the day after (a peak or a trough). The label uses the next day's outcome to choose days to score and is never an input of a forecast
turning_point_days.statistic: the mean absolute error of the forecast median against the actual spread on those days, each model, and the paired twin-minus-published difference with its 90% interval

calibration.statistic: the share of scored days whose actual spread lies inside the band, by regime, each model; the nominal level is 0.50 and 0.90

if_better: a needs-eleonora issue titled "Publish? Direct-pairs training for the published model (#450)" carries the evidence; no published figure moves in the pull request
